result.summary:
REVIEWER, WF-03 step 05 (hard gate) for ISS-0002 (HIGH). VERDICT: PASS. No FAIL-level finding: no bar erosion (Q6/Q10/Q11/Q3 hold), no scope creep, no silent divergence from decisions/0002 or 0004, and no deviation from design v4 behaviour in any of the rows, sweeps and probes listed below. Seven non-blocking findings (F1-F7: one MEDIUM test-design gap, three LOW, three INFO) and the three rulings are below. I changed no code, test or doc; every run used scratch copies; the only file I wrote in the project is this handoff (R2: no agent events written).

REVIEWED. docs/design/REQ-002-idea-verdict.md v4 round 4, sha256 fd2b8f81... (the version BACKEND-DEV built against); REQ-002 block of docs/requirements.yaml re-hashed by me: 39 lines, sha 99b10223 (the one the design maps; criterion 11 present); decisions/0004 sha bda03a34; code: tools/src/apply.js sha fdd0e0b6, prepare.js 66551a90, util.js 8bed1968 (re-hashed at the end: unchanged during my review). Pre-fix copy: I could not reproduce ORCH's manifest hash 2ec4056d (its format is not stated), so I checked it differently: diff -rq pre-fix vs live (node_modules excluded) lists exactly three differing files, apply.js, prepare.js, util.js; the pre-fix line numbers match the references of issue and design (apply.js:100-107 in-place loop, prepare.js:36 existsSync, :133-138 writes); the developer's pristine copies of the three files are byte-identical to ORCH's copy.

SCOPE, EVERY HUNK (diff -u against the pre-fix copy).
- util.js: ONE hunk, @@ -78,4 +78,464 @@: 0 lines removed, lines 1-81 byte-identical (every existing export and listFiles untouched, so snapshot.js is not affected); +460 lines = the write-phase section (isOsError, WriteFailure, addFailure, leftoverFailure, osCall, osError, refused, siblingRel, entryAt, exists, removeEntry, planOf, Journal, inspect W1, stage W2, commit W3, undo, writeAllOrNothing, createFolderAllOrNothing). Nothing else.
- apply.js (5 hunks): (1) import fs removed (now unused); (2) writeAllOrNothing added to the util import; (3) two comment lines on the write phase; (4) the files array replaced by state / proposed / report variables so the commit order [proposed-actions.json, apply-report.json, STATE.md last] can differ from the order of "written" in apply-report.json (that order, STATE.md then proposed-actions.json, is unchanged; report bytes are identical to pre-fix, checked); (5) the existsSync/readFileSync/writeFileSync loop replaced by writeAllOrNothing(root, targets, issues). Return shape { issues, mode, changed } unchanged.
- prepare.js (5 hunks): (1)-(2) imports createFolderAllOrNothing, isOsError; (3) new occupied(): lstat instead of existsSync (any entry, a dangling link included, occupies the run path; an OS error of lstat means "no entry"; any other exception is rethrown); (4) existsSync(runDir) -> occupied(runDir); (5) the mkdir/writeFileSync loop replaced by createFolderAllOrNothing with the copies in run.sources order and run.json last. No pre-fix behaviour is lost: lstat-fails implies stat-fails, so occupied() is true wherever existsSync was.
- Not changed (diff -rq): cli.js, validate.js, snapshot.js, contract.js, clean.js, all of tools/test/, package.json, package-lock.json, eslint.config.js, .prettierignore. No new dependency (decisions/0002: Node 22, none at run time). The three files are the write set of design D6.

FINDINGS (all non-blocking; file:line in the current files).
F1 LOW, tools/src/util.js:298 and :515. The fsync of "flush: true" works only because the options object has no `encoding`. In Node 22.21.1 lib/fs.js writeFileSync, getOptions returns the options object without merging defaults and the C++ fast path for strings tests options.encoding === 'utf8' and passes no flush argument to the binding. My probe (patched fs.fsyncSync, node v22.21.1): { flag: "wx", flush: true } -> fsyncSync called: true; the same plus encoding: "utf8" -> called: false. So the design's measure (§5.2, "flushed to disk") is real today, but one harmless-looking edit would switch it off unnoticed, and no row would fail. Fix: a comment at both calls ("no `encoding` here: with it Node 22 skips the fsync of `flush`") and, for TEST-DESIGNER, one row that counts fs.fsyncSync calls (one per temp file) through the fault-inject module. Not blocking: §5.2 does not promise durability.
F2 LOW (design drift), util.js:106: a third new export, isOsError; §5.7 lists two. See ruling 1.
F3 LOW (design gap, no code change), util.js:180-189 (entryAt) and :464-479 (P1): the <file> of "cannot be checked" is unspecified; the code prints the path whose lstat failed. See ruling 2.
F4 MEDIUM (test-design gap, not a code defect; fix before TEST-DESIGNER maps rows). Design B20/M8 has one row for "a program error is not E_WRITE": W49, apply-verdict only. prepare-run has three places that decide OS error vs program error: prepare.js:30-38 (occupied), util.js:480-484 (P1 catch), util.js:524-539 (P4 catch). I built two mutants on scratch copies: M20a (P4 catch turns any exception into an E_WRITE line) and M20b (occupied swallows every exception). Both pass all of the design's P01-P14 (0 failing) and are caught only by my own program-error rows: PX8 (renameSync of the temp folder -> bug), PX9 (mkdirSync of the temp folder -> bug), PX10 (lstatSync of the run folder -> bug); the live code passes all three (exit 1 by Node, TypeError and trace, no E_WRITE, listing unchanged = cleanup done). Fix (exact design text, Russian as the design): §9.5 two rows, "P15 | runs/ есть | renameSync из runs/.WF06-20260925-01.sai-tmp в <R> - bug | код 1 от Node; stderr содержит `TypeError: injected bug` и строки `    at `; строк E_WRITE нет; stdout пуст; A5 - tree() как до (временная папка убрана) | мутанты" and "P16 | runs/ есть | lstatSync <R> - bug | то же; prepared не напечатано; A5 - tree() как до | мутанты"; §9.7 mutants "M20 в prepare-run любое исключение превращается в E_WRITE (P4) - P15" and "M21 проверка occupied перехватывает всё - P16"; §9.1 B20 tests "W49; P15, P16".
F5 INFO, util.js:439-448 (W4 loop). A program error thrown inside the post-commit cleanup leaves the remaining .sai-old backups (injected TypeError at each of the three unlinks: targets all new, 1-3 backups left, trace, next run names them). Unreachable with the real fs (the paths are valid strings) and consistent with "no catch-all"; the doc comment "Throws only a program error, after rollback and cleanup" is exact for W1-W3 only. No action; optionally one clause in §5.3.
F6 INFO (nit), util.js:103-105: "Nothing in this section catches 'everything'". Syntactically the catch blocks at :429, :480 and :524 do catch everything and then rethrow what is not a WriteFailure after rollback/cleanup, which is right; the sentence reads wrong. Fix: "Nothing here swallows an exception: a non-OS error is rethrown unchanged after rollback and cleanup."
F7 INFO (developer's item 4, pre-existing, not caused by this change). On a scratch copy of the whole real sai/, apply-verdict on the real run WF06-20260926-01 answers "applied recommend", leaves STATE.md unchanged and rewrites only apply-report.json (it records an older STATE.md sha256), with the old code and the new code alike, byte-identical. ORCH should decide before the next real apply-verdict; it is now safe to run (all or nothing).

RULINGS ON THE DEVELOPER'S OPEN QUESTIONS.
1. Third export isOsError (util.js:106). CODE IS RIGHT; the DESIGN needs a small addition (§5.7). prepare.js must treat an lstat error as "no entry" (design §4.1, §5.7: "без исключения наружу") without a catch-all; a bare catch would swallow program errors, which is exactly what mutant M20b is, and the existing bare catch idiom of readTextFile is a read-side convenience, not an example for the write phase. Exact text: in §5.7 replace "два новых экспорта" by "три новых экспорта" and add the table row "`isOsError(err)` | `err` - пойманное исключение | `true`, если у него строковые `code` и `syscall` (так Node описывает ошибки `fs`, §5.3), иначе `false` - ошибка программы. Им пользуется и `prepare.js`: проверка `lstat` пути папки прогона (§4.1) считает «записи нет» только ошибку ОС, любое другое исключение идёт дальше"; in the paragraph after the table drop "признак ошибки ОС (`code` и `syscall` - строки)" from the list of things internal to util.js (it is now an export).
2. <file> in the lines the design is silent about. CODE IS RIGHT. (a) prepare-run's temporary-folder, rename and leftover lines: the design already says it; §5.6 table P2 and P3 "(файл - конечный путь вершины)" and §5.3 defines "вершина" as runs/<RUN-ID>, or runs itself when runs is missing; the code prints exactly that (checked: P05, P06, P10 and, for the runs-missing case, PX1-PX3: "E_WRITE runs: cannot create the temporary folder .runs.sai-tmp (EACCES)", "E_WRITE runs: leftover .runs.sai-tmp ...", "E_WRITE runs: cannot be moved into place (EIO)"). No design change; the only gap is that no row covers the runs-missing top: optional rows, one per line kind. (b) "cannot be checked": the design is silent; the code prints the path whose lstat failed, in every place I forced (apply-verdict: a leftover name, .sai-tmp and .sai-old, the folders runs and runs/<RUN-ID>, the target; prepare-run: runs, its temp folder, and runs with mode 000), e.g. "E_WRITE .STATE.md.sai-tmp: cannot be checked (EIO); nothing was changed", "E_WRITE runs/.WF06-20260925-01.sai-tmp: cannot be checked (EACCES); nothing was changed" (runs mode 000). That is the only reading that tells the reader what failed, since the reason text is fixed. Exact text for the §5.6 table row "W1.1-W1.3, P1 (ошибка lstat, кроме ENOENT) | cannot be checked": add "`<файл>` - путь, чей `lstat` не удался: цель, папка на пути к ней, остаток `.<имя>.sai-tmp` / `.<имя>.sai-old` или временная папка prepare-run". W50 covers only the target; optional rows for the other four.
3. Program-error path with a failing rollback or cleanup. CODE IS RIGHT (design §5.3: rollback and cleanup run, then the exception goes on unchanged); NO ROW is needed; the design needs one sentence so nobody "fixes" it with a catch. Verified (X2, three variants: a TypeError at the STATE.md rename plus EIO at the rollback of apply-report.json; the same plus EIO at the unlink of .STATE.md.sai-old; and one with four OS failures, two rollbacks and two cleanups): exit 1 by Node, TypeError and trace, zero E_WRITE lines, targets old or new (never other), and the leftovers on disk are named by the NEXT run (exit 1, "E_WRITE ...: leftover ... from an interrupted or concurrent run", delete and re-run). So no failure stays silent beyond one run and printing E_WRITE next to a program error would itself be mutant M8. Exact text, §5.3 "Общие правила", after the bullet on program errors: "Если при ошибке программы откат или уборка тоже не удались, строк `E_WRITE` об этом нет: исключение идёт дальше без изменений (трассировка, код 1 от Node), а то, что осталось на диске (`.sai-tmp`, `.sai-old`, цель с новым содержимым и прежним в `.sai-old`), называет следующий запуск строкой «leftover» (W1.3, P1) и отказывает, пока остаток не удалят. Строки теста на это нет."

IS IT A REAL SOLUTION? Yes. It removes both mechanisms at the root, not the symptom: no byte is ever written to a target (M2 gone), the targets change by ordered renames with one commit point and a rollback that needs no write (M1 gone), every handled failure is one E_WRITE line with exit 1, a leftover is refused by name and never deleted by the command, and only OS errors become E_WRITE (a program error keeps its trace, nothing swallows). The evidence is exhaustive injection with a real SIGKILL, not the developer's report.

PROPOSAL TO RAISE THE BAR (quality-bar section 4, one step, optional). For every write phase with a commit point, the tests include an exhaustive sweep (SIGKILL before/after, an OS error and a double fault at every mutating fs call) with the state invariants above. Check: the sweep test exists, passes, and fails on at least three deliberately broken mutants (commit order, rollback, cleanup, leftover check; mine failed 10/15/24/30 times).
